nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the production of greenhouse gas emissions in Sri Lanka differ from the U.S.?
nodes.answer: The production of greenhouse gas emissions in Sri Lanka did not consider building energy use, which underestimates the environmental impact of production compared to the U.S.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How are consumption-based CO2 emissions different from production-based emissions?
nodes.answer: Consumption-based CO2 emissions consider the emissions traded with goods in addition to production-based emissions, providing a more comprehensive view of a country's total emissions impact.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the effect of the scrubber on particle number concentrations at the 20 kW and 60 kW loads?
nodes.answer: The particle number concentrations were reduced by 25% at the 20 kW load and by 38% at the 60 kW load after passing through the scrubber.
nodes.paragraph: Wet scrubbers can impact the environment when wash water is discharged during so-called open-loop operation [9 , 32]. In addition to the efficient removal of SOx, which also reduces secondary sulfate aerosol formation, the air quality benefits include partial scrubbing of water-soluble organic gases, such as carbonyls, thereby reducing the ozone-forming potential of the emissions [7 ]. * Johannes Passig johannes.passig@uni-rostock.de 1 Joint Mass Spectrometry Centre, Analytical Chemistry, University of Rostock, 18059 Rostock, Germany 2 Department Life, Light & Matter, University of Rostock, 18059 Rostock, Germany 3 Faculty for Mechanical Engineering, Institute of Chemistry and Environmental Engineering, University of the Bundeswehr Munich, 85577 Neubiberg, Germany 4 Photonion GmbH, 19061 Schwerin, Germany 5 Chair of Piston Machines and Internal Combustion Engines, University of Rostock, Rostock, Germany 6 Helmholtz Centre Munich, Comprehensive Molecular Analytics, 85764 Neuherberg, Germany 7 Present Address: Atmospheric Chemistry, Leibniz Institute for Tropospheric Research, Leipzig, Germany Environmental Chemistry Letters The reduction in particulate emissions depends on fuel, engine, and scrubber parameters, and consequently, it var - ies in the literature [33, 35] with the majority of the studies indicating only little to moderate effects of the scrubber on particle number and mass emission factors [11, 13].

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which greenhouse gas emissions does the analysis primarily focus on and why?
nodes.answer: The analysis primarily focuses on carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions because they account for the largest share of GHG emissions and are largely by-products of energy consumption.
nodes.paragraph: Also, the NECP envisages the need for higher taxes on heavily polluting activities. The Technical Building Code laysdown new building regulations, to ensure that domestic energy consumption is low. A fundamental driving force behind many of these initiatives will be the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP), presented by the Spanish Government inOctober 2020, which proposes assigning 39% of the funds that Spain receives under the Next Generation EU (NGEU) programme to the green transition; see Cansino et al. (2016) for a description of the policy measures to control carbon emissions in Spain. Ensuring that energy policies are as effective as possible requires an understanding of the main dynamics and drivers of emissions. Within this context, the interest in modelling and forecasting GHG emissions is without doubt. Carbon dioxide (CO 2) emissions, largely by-products of energy consumption, account for the largest share of GHG and, consequently, the analysis of GHG emissions has usually focused on CO 2 emissions; see, for instance, Friedlingstein et al. ( 2022 ), who describes the Global Carbon Project that produces world-wide projections of CO 2emissions in preparing the annual Global Carbon Budget, which is considered in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPPC) reports.
